Subject: Demo on Wed — Meet link says 'You don't have access'

Hi Vivek / Ben,

Thanks for scheduling the demo for Wednesday. Mateo and I just tried to open the calendar invite that came through and the Google Meet link returns a 'You don't have access to this meeting' page — both of us are on external domains. I've attached a screenshot of the error.

We don't want to miss the slot, but we also can't accept an invite that won't let us join. Can you either:
- resend with a Zoom link, or
- set the organizer to the Redwood host so guests have join permissions

Prefer to keep the scheduled slot (Apr 7, 11:00 PDT) if possible; otherwise we can move to 12:30 or 14:00 PDT.

Attached: screenshot-meet-error.png (image/png)

Best,

Hi Sarah / Mateo — really sorry about that.

Thanks for the screenshot — looks like the invite was created with an organizer alias that doesn't allow external guests through Meet. To unblock immediately I've created a Zoom bridge and attached an .ics with the new info. Please use the Zoom link below for Wednesday's session:  https://zoom.us/j/999888777 (passcode: 4213).

If Wednesday 11:00 PDT still works, we'll keep that slot and I'll confirm attendees. If you'd prefer 12:30 or 14:00, let me know and I'll update the calendar.

Attachments: zoom-bridge.ics (calendar/ics)

Apologies for the extra step — we should have the organizer issue fixed for future invites.

-Vivek

Quick note on what happened here — our CRM auto-creates calendar events using the sales-assist alias (lauren+biz@redwood.com) for routing. That alias was set as the organizer which, for cross-domain guests, can strip join permissions on Google Meet.

Workaround: easiest is for Lauren to create a fresh event as the host (or forward an event where she is organizer) or we push a Zoom bridge as Vivek already did. I'll follow up with Platform to remove the alias-as-organizer behavior but for this demo let's send the Zoom invite and ask the prospect to accept that event.

Ben
